correctness.rationale: PASS: In PG(d-1,q), q any prime power >=2, d>=2, singletons are closed and every pair is a pseudo-intent because its line has q+1 points. A larger pseudo-intent would contain the closure of every pair and hence be a projective flat, contradiction. For synchronous one-pass closure, each independent A and full-support point p in its span has no proper-subset rule capable of adding p in that pass; therefore the premise A and root p are compulsory. Conversely minimal spanning support of any target point is independent, making those rules sufficient. Count independent r-subsets I_r=prod_j(N-N_j)/r!, and full-support roots (q-1)^(r-1), deriving both exact grouped/unit formulas. Induction on rounds with a balanced partition of support establishes R_t(S)=union of spans over supports of size <=2^t. A rank-r independent frame and its all-nonzero coordinate sum attain ceil(log2 r); general rank-r inputs achieve closure by then. Independently enumerated all 128 subsets PG(2,2) and 8192 subsets PG(2,3), checking pair pseudo-intents, direct rule counts (21/49 and 78/312, unit 1092), closure and rounds. The independent finite tests cover q=2,3,d=3; all prime powers and dimensions rest on proof.
